entries.fix_shape: Raise on LLMErrorEvent/exception (the engine already turns raises into node-error); drop config api_key and thread the foreground BYOK creds from the run request like agents.invoke does; pass a BudgetGuard on_round_usage callback; move the CI stub into the test fixture. entries.title: Concurrent quant pricings corrupt each other through QuantLib's process-global evaluation date (a valid call priced at 0.0 in 1413 of 3000 overlapping runs), and the async quant agent tools price synchronously on the event loop
entries.repro: [COD-macro-quant-2] Two threads call services.quant._common.set_evaluation_date with different dates then read ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate: thread A set 2026-05-16, thread B set 2030-01-02, both observe 'January 2nd, 2030'. The four /quant routes are plain sync `def`, so FastAPI runs them concurrently in the anyio worker threadpool -> two simultaneous pricing calls with different valuation_date can each be served the other's date.
entries.evidence: [COD-macro-quant-2] sidecar/services/quant/_common.py:34-41 (set_evaluation_date writes the process global), _common.py:57 (build_bsm_process calls it on every price), sidecar/services/quant/bonds.py:52 and sidecar/services/quant/yield_curve.py:70 (write it directly), sidecar/routers/quant.py:37,46,55,64 (all four routes are sync `def`, unlike routers/macro.py:47,60,72 which are async def) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (critical->high): Mechanism is real and worse than a date mix-up: the four /quant routes are sync def (threadpool) and every engine writes the process-global ql.Settings evaluationDate before a lazy NPV(); a two-thread probe returned price 0.0 (option judged already expired) for 1413 of 3000 pricings of a valid ITM-ish call when a second thread priced with a later valuation date. Severity corrected critical->high only because the trigger needs two overlapping quant computations with DIFFERENT valuation dates in a single-user desktop (panel computes are click-driven; the async agent tools call options.price synchronously on the event loop, quant_tools.py:54, which also blocks the loop for large binomial_steps).
entries.root_cause: ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate is a process singleton; the four /quant routes are sync def (anyio threadpool) and every engine writes the global before a lazy NPV(), so two overlapping pricings with different valuation dates read each other's date.
entries.fix_shape: Module-level threading.Lock in _common.py wrapping set-date-through-NPV as one critical section (used by options, greeks, bonds, yield_curve), plus await asyncio.to_thread(...) in the four quant_tools handlers. Pin with the two-thread probe as a pytest. Must land before/with R15-CODE-PLATFORM entry for quant workflow nodes (moving those to to_thread without the lock makes this race reachable from workflows too).

entries.title: Registered kill-switch chord is Ctrl+Cmd+Shift+K (all three modifiers AND-ed), not the documented CmdOrCtrl+Shift+K, so the emergency chord never matches while an OS-wide chord is grabbed for a dead event

entries.fix_shape: Refuters established the kill switch gates ONLY broker order placement (sole subscriber BrokerAdapter.__init__, sidecar/services/broker_base.py:103; sole is_fired readers the propose/confirm gates, broker_base.py:251,345) and the audit log has only trading writers. entries.title: write_text_atomic / write_bytes_atomic accept any absolute path from the webview with no confinement, and CSP is null, so any webview script can write arbitrary bytes anywhere the user can write

entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-5] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:287-310 (write_text_atomic) and :318-342 (write_bytes_atomic) — no path validation; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:410-411 (both in the production invoke_handler); src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.security.csp = null; the guard lives in callers and only in some of them: src/modules/notes/notes-persistence.ts:68 strips [/\\] from the scope, src/lib/export-artifact.ts:76-88 interpolates subdir + filename straight in; docs/research/phase-10/hunt-rust-tauri.md 'SECURITY HARDENING — csp: null' reported the CSP half and it is unfixed at 2d99cda -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): The missing boundary is real: write_text_atomic/write_bytes_atomic take any path and only create_dir_all the parent (lib.rs:287-342), they are in the release invoke_handler (lib.rs:410-411), app commands are unrestricted (no AppManifest in build.rs), and CSP is null. Corrected on two particulars: (1) 'one caller already forgot' is wrong in effect - export-artifact.ts saveTextArtifact interpolates subdir/filename unsanitised, but its only callers (NotesPanel.tsx:225,236,247) pass the constant 'notes' and a base name sanitised at NotesPanel.tsx:220; (2) the plugin threat model cited does not exist today - plugins are static bundled imports (plugin-runtime.ts:26-28, marketplace.ts:8-41), not runtime-loaded third-party JS, and the finder itself found no injection sink. entries.root_cause: Path confinement was pushed up into callers (notes-persistence sanitises, export-artifact interpolates) instead of held by the command; no CSP backstop. No live injection vector today (no innerHTML sinks, plugins are static imports).
entries.fix_shape: One private write_atomic(path, bytes) that canonicalises the parent and rejects anything outside app_data_dir(); both commands become one line over it (collapses the write_atomic duplication entry). entries.title: Plugin Manager enable/disable toggle lies: disable stops the instance in memory only (back after restart, panels/commands/agents never leave) and enable of a Marketplace-disabled plugin is a no-op
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-1] Open the Plugin Manager panel -> flip any active plugin's toggle off -> restart the app. The plugin is active again. Before restarting: its panels/slash commands are still in cmd+K and its agents still in the chat roster.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-1] src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:171-185 (calls runtime.unloadPlugin directly), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:278-295 (unloadPlugin touches no persistence), src/store/marketplace.ts:176-191 (the sibling path calls disablePlugin + unbridgePluginModule + syncPluginAgents(false) + disconnectBroker), src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:262-264 (boot re-reads plugins.db, which still says enabled:true) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Real: PluginRow.handleToggle calls runtime.loadPlugin/unloadPlugin directly; unloadPlugin persists nothing, so boot re-reads enabled:true and reloads it, and no unbridge/agent-sync runs. The reverse direction is also dead: toggling ON a Marketplace-disabled plugin is a no-op because loadPlugin honours persisted enabled:false. Severity corrected high->medium: the designated lifecycle surface (Marketplace store enable/disable) is correct; this is a second, lying control on a secondary panel, not a broken core flow.
entries.root_cause: The panel calls the runtime primitives (loadPlugin/unloadPlugin) while the Marketplace store calls the policies (disablePlugin + unbridge + syncPluginAgents + persistence).
entries.fix_shape: Route PluginRow.handleToggle through useMarketplaceStore.enable/disable; structural: move persist+bridge+agent-sync into PluginRuntime.enable/disable so every caller is thin. Pin with a test that toggling off persists enabled:false and unbridges the module.

entries.title: 'Is this plugin on?' lives in two independent stores (plugins.db enabled and workspace enabledModules['plugin:<id>']) that only one of three code paths keeps in sync; restoring an older named workspace hides the panels of a plugin re-enabled since
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-12] design (drift hazard, reachable via COD-plugins-1): plugins.db `enabled` and the workspace blob's enabledModules['plugin:<id>'] are written by different callers; disable via the Plugin Manager writes neither, disable via the runtime writes only the first, unbridgePluginModule writes only the second.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-12] sidecar/services/plugins_store.py:38-44 (plugins.db enabled column), src/lib/workspace.ts:50,263 (workspace.enabledModules -> setEnabledMap replaces the map wholesale on restore), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:344-348 (disablePlugin writes only plugins.db), src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:193-194 (unbridgePluginModule writes only the module map), src/store/marketplace.ts:182-183 (the only caller that writes both). Four sites encode the never-persisted default and disagree: plugin-runtime.ts:221, plugin-runtime.ts:310, plugin-bootstrap.ts:262-263, store/marketplace.ts:109-110/123-125 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Holds: plugins.db enabled and the workspace blob's enabledModules['plugin:<id>'] are independent; disablePlugin writes only the former, unbridgePluginModule only the latter, and workspace restore replaces the whole enabled map (so an older named workspace carrying plugin:x=false hides panels of a plugin re-enabled since). The never-persisted default is spelled at four sites with two answers.
entries.root_cause: No single owner for the enabled fact; the never-persisted default is spelled at four sites with two different answers (true vs row.entry.preinstalled).
entries.fix_shape: One lifecycle owner writes both, or derive the module-enabled flag from runtime state instead of persisting it in the workspace blob; one shared default. Pin with a test restoring a workspace blob with plugin:x=false over a re-enabled plugin.

entries.title: Saving a BYOK secret for an already-active plugin never re-runs initialize(), so PluginConfig.secrets stays stale until restart (and a green test locks the no-op)
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-3] Marketplace -> Configure any plugin that is already active (e.g. vysted-news, preinstalled+enabled) -> save a key. The keychain write lands and grantedSecretIds is persisted, but initialize() is never called again, so the running instance keeps the secrets map it got at boot (empty).
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-3] src/store/marketplace.ts:238-244 (comment: 'Reload so the plugin resolves the new secrets via PluginConfig.secrets' -> calls runtime.enablePlugin), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:339-342 (enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:199-202 (loadPlugin returns early when state is 'active'), src/lib/plugin-runtime.test.ts:171-177 (green test locks the no-op: initialize called once after two loadPlugin calls), types/plugin.ts:41-42 (PluginConfig.secrets is the contract's designated credential channel) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Mechanism holds: configure() calls enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin, which returns early for an active record, so initialize() never re-runs and PluginConfig.secrets stays stale; the green test locks that idempotence. Severity corrected high->medium because it is latent: no bundled plugin reads config.secrets for a credential (only plugins/example reports the key ids), vysted-news reads its key out-of-band, and the broker consumers are being removed.
entries.root_cause: configure() calls enablePlugin -> patchConfig -> loadPlugin, which returns early for an active record; the comment claims a reload.
entries.fix_shape: Add a real runtime.reloadPlugin() (unload then load) and call it from configure(); update the test that asserts initialize() is called once to assert it re-runs after configure. Latent: no bundled plugin reads config.secrets for a credential yet.

entries.title: Plugin data contribution is declaration-only: getDataSources() output only feeds a count in the Plugin Manager subtitle, VystedPlugin.subscribe has no host call site, so DataSource.realtime cannot be honoured and a data plugin cannot serve one quote
entries.repro: [INT-blueprint-48-5] Write a plugin with `contributesData: true` and a DataSource; it loads, and the only effect anywhere in the app is the count in the plugin-manager subtitle (`${dataSources.length} data sources`, src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:42). No panel, store or sidecar route resolves a read through a plugin-contributed source. The bundled reference plugin says so in its own header: 'The actual data flows through the sidecar's provider_registry (this plugin is a thin declaration of the source...)' (plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11). Likewise `VystedPlugin.subscribe` (types/plugin.ts:251) has no host call site in src/ and no implementor in plugins/, so `DataSource.realtime: true` (types/plugin.ts:84) cannot be honoured.
entries.evidence: [INT-blueprint-48-5] types/plugin.ts:76-87,236,251; src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:419-425; src/store/plugins.ts:62,86; src/components/PluginManagerPanel.tsx:28,42; plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11; plugins/openbb-mcp/index.ts:168 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Holds. getDataSources() output goes only into the plugins store (plugin-runtime.ts:422, store/plugins.ts:62,86), and its only reader is the PluginManagerPanel count (PluginManagerPanel.tsx:28,42). Nothing in src/ calls `VystedPlugin.subscribe`: the runtime's own `subscribe` (plugin-runtime.ts:525) is a UI-listener API. So `DataSource.realtime` (types/plugin.ts:86) cannot be honoured, and yfinance/index.ts:1-11 admits the plugin is a declaration only. This does not reopen the plugin system's existence; it is an inert contract slice.
entries.root_cause: The data slice of the contract was never wired to a resolution seam; actual data flows only through the sidecar provider_registry (plugins/yfinance/index.ts:1-11 admits it).
entries.fix_shape: Operator choice (contract honesty is Tier-4): either a resolution seam (provider_registry entry backed by a plugin-declared sidecar route) or document DataSource as a declaration and mark realtime/subscribe reserved in types/plugin.ts + PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT.md. Pin with a test that a declared source is either resolvable or flagged not-runnable.

entries.title: The Notify Desktop workflow node never produces an OS notification: the bridge reads useWorkflowStore, which no production code writes to
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-5] Run a workflow containing action.notify_desktop from the node editor -> NodeEditorPanel consumes SSE with its own consumeSse + local setRunState and never calls useWorkflowStore.appendEvent -> pendingNotifications stays empty -> useDesktopNotificationBridge (mounted in page.tsx:43) never fires.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-5] src/store/workflow.ts:173-192,203-220,240-311 (the only intent capture + a second full SSE client); grep: no production caller of runWorkflow/appendEvent outside src/store/workflow.ts (only src/lib/desktop-notification.ts reads the slice); src/modules/node-editor/NodeEditorPanel.tsx:386-431,937-976 (separate SSE parser); src/app/page.tsx:43; sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:325-344 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): No production code calls useWorkflowStore.appendEvent or runWorkflow: the only consumer of the store is the notification bridge (src/lib/desktop-notification.ts), while NodeEditorPanel runs its own fetch + consumeSse + local setRunState. The bridge mounted in page.tsx therefore never receives an intent, so the Notify Desktop node never produces an OS notification.
entries.root_cause: Two SSE clients / run-state models for one wire; NodeEditorPanel runs its own consumeSse + local state while the notification bridge listens to the dead store (376 lines, unit-tested in isolation).
entries.fix_shape: NodeEditorPanel dispatches every server event through useWorkflowStore.appendEvent (or calls the intent capture directly); delete the store's unused runWorkflow SSE client and dead clearRun/clearAll. Pin with a NodeEditorPanel test that a notify_desktop node-complete event enqueues a notification.

entries.title: transform.code has two evaluators with different semantics: the editor (mathjs) and the agent/MCP path (Python ast) disagree on round(2.5), '^' and ternaries for the same saved workflow
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-6] round(2.5): mathjs 3 vs server 2; 2^3: mathjs 8 vs server 'disallowed syntax: BinOp'; 'a > 1 ? 1 : 0': mathjs 1 vs server parse error (both measured). A workflow authored and tested in the editor then run by the agent via MCP run_workflow yields a different value or fails.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-6] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/code_node.py:20-45,97 (Python round = banker's rounding, '^' unsupported, no ternary); src/modules/node-editor/code-node.ts:1-27 (mathjs); stale comments claiming no server handler exists: src/modules/node-editor/code-node.ts:26-27, src/modules/node-editor/code-node-run.ts:12-15; now-obsolete restriction: code-node-run.ts:63-74; sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:258-285 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): The server lane really is a separate Python-ast evaluator with different semantics (banker's rounding, '^' parsed as BitXor and rejected, no ternary), and the client comments claiming no server handler exists are stale since code_node.register() is called from register_all. The code_node.py header does document the '^' gap, but round() divergence is silent and the client partition restriction is now obsolete.
entries.root_cause: Two implementations shipped and never compared; client comments still claim no server handler exists, so the client partition (code nodes evaluate after the stream, code->server edges forbidden) is obsolete.
entries.fix_shape: Run transform.code only on the server (keep mathjs for inline syntax preview at most), drop the partition restriction and the stale comments; if both stay, a shared parity fixture both suites evaluate.

entries.title: Quant workflow nodes run CPU-bound pricing synchronously on the sidecar event loop (Monte Carlo up to 10M paths, binomial up to 100k steps), freezing every sidecar route for the duration
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-8] A workflow with quant.price_option {method: 'monte-carlo', monte_carlo_paths: 10000000} (MAX_MC_PATHS) or binomial_steps up to 100000 -> options.price runs inline in the async handler, freezing the whole sidecar for the duration.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-8] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/quant_nodes.py:46-52,57-63,68-74,79-85 (sync calls, no to_thread); sidecar/models/quant.py:33-34 (MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS=100_000, MAX_MC_PATHS=10_000_000); contrast sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/builtin.py:62-64,87-89,121 (to_thread) and sidecar/routers/quant.py:36-37 (sync def -> threadpool) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): All four quant adapters call options.price / greeks / bonds / yield_curve synchronously inside async handlers, while the builtin adapters use asyncio.to_thread and the HTTP /quant routes are sync defs (threadpool). Parameters up to MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS=100000 (binomial prices ~9 trees for FD greeks) and MAX_MC_PATHS=10M are accepted as valid, so a user-permitted config stalls the whole sidecar loop.
entries.root_cause: The four quant adapters call options/greeks/bonds/yield_curve inline in async handlers, unlike the builtin adapters (to_thread) and the /quant HTTP routes (threadpool).
entries.fix_shape: asyncio.to_thread around each quant call (four one-line changes), landing with or after the QuantLib evaluation-date lock (else the date race becomes reachable here); ideally the engine runs every handler off-loop under a per-node timeout. Pin with a test that a long pricing does not block a concurrent /health.

entries.title: Workflow engine has no per-node or per-run timeout and schedules in gather-barrier waves, so a slow node stalls unrelated dependants and a hung handler keeps the run (and the MCP run_workflow call) open forever
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-9] Sources A (flow.sleep 300 s or a hung provider fetch) and B (fast); C depends only on B -> C does not start until A finishes because each wave is awaited with asyncio.gather. A handler that never returns keeps the run (and the MCP run_workflow tool call) open indefinitely.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-9] sidecar/services/workflow_engine.py:3-5 (docstring: 'runs downstream nodes when their inputs are available'), :210-282 (ready-set recomputed only after the whole wave's gather), :366-367 (await handler with no wait_for); sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:282-283 (no timeout around run_workflow) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): The scheduler recomputes the ready set only after asyncio.gather of the whole wave, so a slow node delays unrelated dependants, and the handler call has no wait_for; the MCP run_workflow tool awaits the engine with no timeout either. Only flow.sleep has a bound (300 s).
entries.root_cause: The ready set is recomputed only after asyncio.gather of the whole wave; handlers are awaited without wait_for; the docstring says the opposite.
entries.fix_shape: Schedule with asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) so each completion releases its dependants, and wrap each handler in asyncio.wait_for(node_timeout) producing node-error; pin with an A(slow)/B(fast)/C<-B test asserting C starts before A ends.

entries.title: Saved workflows have no schema versioning: one row that no longer validates makes GET /workflow/saved 500 and the Load dialog shows no workflow at all
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-10] A row whose spec_json no longer validates (a field removed/renamed in a later release, or any extra key — every model is extra='forbid') -> list_workflows validates all rows in one comprehension -> ValidationError -> 500 -> Load dialog shows 'list failed (500)' and no workflow is loadable.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-10] sidecar/services/workflow_store.py:53-63; sidecar/models/workflow.py:23,32,43,55 (extra='forbid'), :60 (version stored, never checked); types/workflow.ts:65 ('the engine refuses unknown majors' — not implemented anywhere); src/modules/node-editor/NodeEditorPanel.tsx:292-295 -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): list_workflows validates every row in one comprehension against extra='forbid' models with no try/skip, spec.version is stored but never checked, and types/workflow.ts:65's 'engine refuses unknown majors' is unimplemented. No current write path produces a bad row (save goes through the same model), so this is latent - it bites at the first schema change, which the medium bar ('bites the next maintainer') covers.
entries.root_cause: list_workflows validates every row in one comprehension against extra='forbid' models; spec.version is stored but never checked (types/workflow.ts:65's 'engine refuses unknown majors' is unimplemented).
entries.fix_shape: Skip-and-log rows that fail validation (return them as 'needs migration' summaries) and check spec.version on load with an explicit migrate step; pin with a store test inserting one bad row and asserting the rest still list.

entries.title: Portfolio risk analytics promised under Portfolio & Risk (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, VaR, Beta, max drawdown, correlation matrix) do not exist for the user's tracked portfolio; 4 of 7 exist only inside the backtest engine and VaR/Beta/correlation exist nowhere

entries.evidence: [INT-blueprint-96-2] sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:236-282 (sharpe/sortino/calmar computed only for a backtest run); sidecar/models/portfolio.py (position model: no risk fields); sidecar/services/portfolio_db.py (no risk computation); docs/BLUEPRINT.md:266 "Risk analytics (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, VaR, Beta, max drawdown, correlation matrix)" listed under Portfolio & Risk, not Backtesting -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Confirmed VaR/Beta/correlation-matrix are absent sidecar-wide (not just in portfolio code), and that Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/max-drawdown are computed only inside backtest_engine.py against a simulated equity curve, never against the user's actual tracked-portfolio return series in portfolio_db.py/models/portfolio.py. The promise sits under 'Portfolio & Risk' in BLUEPRINT.md's own module catalog, not under Backtesting, so grading it against the live portfolio (where it is 0% built for 3 of 7 metrics and 100% absent for the rest) is the right frame, not a misread of scope.
entries.root_cause: The risk-metric promise was only ever met by the backtest module on a simulated equity curve.
entries.fix_shape: Either compute the metrics on the tracked portfolio's return series (client-side in metrics.ts over price history, since the sidecar portfolio store is slated for deletion) and surface them in the panel with tests, or correct BLUEPRINT.md to scope risk analytics to backtests.

entries.title: BLUEPRINT's 'Rust layer provides file system access' is not implemented: no fs capability or plugin is granted and the only user file-write flow (portfolio CSV export) is a webview Blob download
entries.repro: [INT-blueprint-0-7] cat src-tauri/capabilities/default.json -> permissions = [core:default, global-shortcut:allow-is-registered, notification:default, shell:allow-open], no fs:*; grep tauri-plugin-fs src-tauri/Cargo.toml package.json -> 0 hits
entries.evidence: [INT-blueprint-0-7] src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:6-11; src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:9,504 (imports downloadCsv from src/lib/csv.ts, a webview Blob/anchor download, not a Tauri fs write) -- refuter admitted (medium->medium): Re-verified independently: capabilities/default.json's permission list has no fs:* entry, neither tauri-plugin-fs nor @tauri-apps/plugin-fs appears in Cargo.toml/package.json, and lib.rs's full .plugin() chain (shell/updater/notification/kill_switch/mcp) confirms fs was never registered. entries.fix_shape: Either grant a scoped fs capability and wire a real save-to-path flow for exports, or correct BLUEPRINT.md §3.1 to describe the browser-download mechanism.

entries.title: audit-design-tokens.mjs resolves ROOT via URL.pathname, which is invalid on Windows, so the audit walks zero files and prints 'design-token audit clean'

entries.evidence: [COD-scripts-build-6] scripts/audit-design-tokens.mjs:23 (const ROOT = new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname), :75-81 (statSync(abs) in try/catch -> continue), :121 (console.log("design-token audit clean")), :62 (SKIP_FILES = new Set(["styles/tokens.css"]) compared against relative() output which is backslash-separated on Windows, and dead anyway under the default SCAN at :27). entries.title: Backtest engine credits a sell larger than the held position in full and pops the whole position, minting cash from phantom shares

Result: final equity 108989 from initialCapital 100000 on a market that never moved; the trade's reported pnl is -19.99 (fees only), so nothing in the trade log or metrics hints that 90 phantom shares were sold.
entries.evidence: [COD-backtest-4] sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:362-365 (position looked up, then `portfolio.cash += abs(intent.quantity) * fill_price` with no reconciliation against position.quantity), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:371 (pnl computed on abs(intent.quantity)), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:385 (`portfolio.positions.pop(...)` regardless of size), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:368-370 (comment parks the partial-close case as a 'documented limitation') -- refuter admitted_with_correction (high->medium): Mechanism confirmed (sell credits abs(intent.quantity) with no reconciliation against position.quantity, then pops the whole position), but, as with COD-backtest-3, every registered strategy exits with quantity=-held, so no shipped path (UI, custom DSL, agent tool) can over-sell. entries.title: Chat SSE consumer relabels consumer exceptions as 'unparseable SSE frame', and a stream that ends without a done/error frame leaves the message streaming, the run 'running' and the brief in_flight forever
entries.repro: [COD-error-layer-11] design: handlers.onEvent(event) is inside the same try as JSON.parse (streaming.ts:263-271). A throw in ChatSidebar's onToolUse/enqueueChange or in feedBriefLifecycle (called from normalizeEvent) is caught, relabelled `unparseable SSE frame: <consumer message>`, routed to onError -> the assistant message is failed and the run ended as 'error' while the stream keeps delivering frames to a settled message. SECOND HALF (design): consumeSseStream returns normally when reader.read() reports done (streaming.ts:225-244) whether or not a terminal frame was seen; ChatSidebar settles a turn ONLY in onDone/onError (ChatSidebar.tsx:890-939) and does nothing after `await streamAgentInvocation(...)` (:1005-1038). Any server path that closes the generator without `done` leaves the message 'streaming', the rail run 'running', abortRef held and the brief panel in_flight, forever.
entries.evidence: [COD-error-layer-11] src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:263-271, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:302-305 (store side effect inside normalizeEvent), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:890-912, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:225-249 (no sawTerminal tracking), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:914-939,1005-1038, src/modules/chat/streaming.test.ts (10 tests; none for non-ok, malformed frame, consumer throw, or EOF-without-done) -- refuter admitted (low->low): Holds on both halves: dispatchFrame wraps JSON.parse, normalizeEvent (which calls feedBriefLifecycle) and handlers.onEvent in one try and relabels any throw 'unparseable SSE frame: …'; consumeSseStream returns normally on reader done without tracking a terminal frame, and ChatSidebar settles only in onDone/onError with nothing after the await.
entries.root_cause: dispatchFrame wraps JSON.parse, normalizeEvent (which mutates the brief store) and handlers.onEvent in one try; consumeSseStream does not track a terminal frame and ChatSidebar settles only in onDone/onError.

entries.title: LLMProvider.stream_chat is declared 'async def -> AsyncIterator' (a coroutine) while all five adapters and all three callers treat it as an async generator
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-0-4] sidecar/services/llm/base.py:83-90 declares '@abstractmethod async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[LLMStreamEvent]'. Every concrete adapter (anthropic.py:103, gemini.py:99, groq.py:101, ollama.py:126, openai.py:656) is an async-generator function (contains 'yield' directly in its async def body). The only call site, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1434, does 'async for event in adapter.stream_chat(...)' with no 'await' before it -- correct for an async generator, but inconsistent with what the ABC's 'async def' signature would imply (call, then await the coroutine to get the iterator).
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-0-4] sidecar/services/llm/base.py:83-90, sidecar/services/llm/anthropic.py:103, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1434 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The mismatch is real: base.py:85-108 is an abstract 'async def' whose body is just 'raise NotImplementedError' (no yield), so it declares a coroutine, while all five adapters are async generators. Two corrections. There are three call sites, not one: agent_runtime.py:1434, native_search.py:242 and oneshot.py:79, and all of them iterate without await. Severity also drops to low, because no type checker runs anywhere (no mypy/pyright config or CI step), so nothing enforces the ABC. Nothing changes at runtime; this is a one-word annotation fix.
entries.root_cause: The ABC's abstract body has no yield; no type checker runs to catch the mismatch.
entries.fix_shape: Drop `async` from the base declaration (BLOCKERS.md's named fix) or add a `yield` after the raise.

entries.title: Boot path bridges a plugin's panels and commands without checking that loadPlugin succeeded, so an errored plugin still contributes UI
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-5] Make any bundled plugin's initialize() throw (or drift its manifest version from its instance version, which checkCompatibility rejects) -> restart. The Plugin Manager renders the row red 'error' while its panels and slash commands are live in cmd+K.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-5] src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:264-270 (`await runtime.loadPlugin(plugin)` return value discarded, then appendModules unconditionally), vs the three guarded siblings src/store/marketplace.ts:147, :165, :241 (`if (snap.state === 'active')`), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:356-365 (documents the FR-054/SC-015 'contributes nothing' promise), src/lib/plugin-runtime.test.ts:516 ('an incompatible plugin contributes nothing' -- asserted at the runtime level only) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Core claim holds: the boot loop discards loadPlugin's snapshot and appendModules unconditionally (modules default enabled), unlike the three guarded store paths. Mechanism corrected: the cited hardcoded versions at marketplace.ts:91/125/140 are MarketplaceEntry.version, which checkCompatibility never reads, and manifest/instance version drift for bundled rows is CI-guarded by marketplace.test.ts:44; the reachable first-party path is a transient persistence.load failure at boot (config-load error) or an initialize() throw. Severity medium->low: plugins are compiled in, and after broker removal only vysted-example contributes commands and none contribute panels.
entries.root_cause: The boot loop discards loadPlugin's snapshot, unlike the three guarded store paths.
entries.fix_shape: const snap = await runtime.loadPlugin(plugin); bridge only if snap.state === 'active'; pin with a bootstrap test where initialize() throws.

entries.title: moduleForPlugin re-implements capability negotiation without the runtime's try/catch, so a throwing getPanels()/getCommands() rejects bootstrapPlugins() mid-loop
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-6] A plugin whose getPanels() or getCommands() throws: runtime.collectPanels() contains it and emits `errored`, but moduleForPlugin lets it propagate -> the unguarded call at plugin-bootstrap.ts:266 rejects bootstrapPlugins() and the plugin layer never finishes booting. Same throw also breaks bridge/unbridge on disable.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-6] src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:135-138 (flag -> optional getter, no try/catch) vs src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:389-416 (callIfFlagged: flag check + getter-exists check + `errored` emit + try/catch), unguarded callers at src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:183, :198, :266 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real duplication: moduleForPlugin calls getPanels/getCommands with no try/catch or missing-getter errored event, while callIfFlagged has both; a throw at plugin-bootstrap.ts:266 would reject bootstrapPlugins mid-loop (page.tsx only .then()s it). Severity medium->low: every plugin is compiled in, and post-trading-removal the only panel/command contributor is plugins/example with a static getCommands array, so the throw path is latent.
entries.root_cause: The flag->getter rule is written twice; the copy lacks callIfFlagged's guard and errored event.
entries.fix_shape: Source panels/commands from runtime.collectPanels()/collectCommands() filtered by plugin id (or export callIfFlagged); collapse the five collect* bodies to one collect<T>. Pin with a throwing-getter test.

entries.title: healthCheckOne writes back a pre-await snapshot, reverting a disable/error transition that lands during the health check to 'active'
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-10] Disable a plugin (or have it transition to error) while its healthCheck() promise is in flight: the health poll then writes {...staleRecord, healthHistory} over the map entry, restoring state:'active' and clearing the errorMessage/stateChangedAt that were just written.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-10] src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:478-499 (record captured from the activePlugins() snapshot at :473, awaited at :484, wholesale `this.plugins.set(record.manifest.id, {...record, healthHistory: newHistory})` at :496), src/lib/plugin-bootstrap.ts:40,273-276 (poll armed every 30s, plus one immediately at boot) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The lost update is real: healthCheckOne captures the record from activePlugins() before awaiting healthCheck() and writes {...record, healthHistory} back, overwriting any transition (stopping/stopped/error) that landed during the await. Severity medium->low: the bundled healthChecks are a loopback GET /health (or synchronous), so the window is milliseconds every 30s, and a stale 'active' is corrected by the persisted enabled:false on next launch.
entries.root_cause: Lost update: full-record overwrite of state captured before an await.
entries.fix_shape: Re-read this.plugins.get(id) after the await and bail if gone or no longer active, or mutate only healthHistory; pin with a test disabling during a pending healthCheck.

entries.title: parseSemver strips '<' with the range operators, inverting a '<x.y.z' requiredHostVersion into '>=x.y.z' (and the error message hardcodes '>=')
entries.repro: [COD-plugins-14] A manifest with requiredHostVersion "<0.9.0" on host 0.8.0 is REJECTED at load with the message 'plugin requires host version >= <0.9.0 but host is 0.8.0' -- the opposite of what the manifest asked for.
entries.evidence: [COD-plugins-14] src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:116-125 (`version.trim().replace(/^[\^~>=<\s]+/, "")` -- '<' is in the stripped class), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:133-139 (hostSatisfies then compares with >=), src/lib/plugin-runtime.ts:374-376 (the error message hardcodes '>=' regardless of the operator that was stripped) -- refuter admitted (low->low): parseSemver's stripped class includes '<', so '<0.9.0' parses as 0.9.0 and hostSatisfies applies >=, inverting the constraint, and the error message hardcodes '>='. Latent: bundled manifests use bare x.y.z or '>=0.4.0'.
entries.root_cause: '<' is in the stripped character class while ranges are documented as unsupported.
entries.fix_shape: Drop '<' from the class so an unsupported operator fails loudly; pin with a manifest test for '<0.9.0'.

entries.title: Removing a credentialed non-broker plugin (e.g. vysted-news) never deletes its plugin-secret keychain entry, and the legacy vysted-search-exa secret has no cleanup
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-84-5] install a search-tier backend with a key (e.g. Exa) -> disable or remove it -> plugin-secret:<id> keychain entry is never deleted, only manual Keychain Access cleanup removes it
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-84-5] src/store/marketplace.ts:175-204 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The mechanism is real, but the subject and scope are wrong. No 'search-tier plugin' exists: the Exa/R7-R8 search lanes are dead (search-headers.ts:27-30) and the marketplace catalog has no search entry. The actual gap is that `remove()` on ANY credentialed non-broker plugin (e.g. vysted-news `plugin-secret:vysted-news:newsapi_key`) never calls deleteSecret. runtime.removePlugin only patches config and unloads, and disconnectBroker is broker-only and does not touch the keychain. Leaving the secret on `disable()` is correct: disable is reversible and the plugin stays installed. The legacy `plugin-secret:vysted-search-exa` orphan also has no migration that cleans it. The secret stays in the user's own OS keychain and is never exposed, so low.
entries.root_cause: remove() only patches config and unloads; disconnectBroker is broker-only and does not touch the keychain.
entries.fix_shape: remove() calls deleteSecret for each granted plugin-secret id (disable() correctly keeps it); one-shot migration deleting the dead exa secret; pin with a marketplace store test.

entries.title: updateHolding's interface comment says 'Patch' but it replaces, turning an absent numeric into 0 (a zeroed cost basis for any future untyped caller)
entries.repro: [COD-portfolio-14] design — a caller trusting the word "Patch" and passing {symbol, quantity} would get costBasis 0 (Number(undefined) -> NaN -> 0). TypeScript's required HoldingInput prevents it from a typed caller today, so the defect is in the comment, not yet in behaviour.

The interface comment at 105 says 'Patch an existing holding.' while updateHolding rebuilds the holding from input via normalizeHolding (a missing numeric becomes 0). The sibling updatePosition doc at 239-246 states the replace semantics correctly. The typed HoldingInput prevents misuse today, so this is doc-only, low.

entries.title: PortfolioSummary.concentration is computed from cross-currency weights and returned unflagged; only the panel knows to withhold it
entries.repro: [COD-portfolio-15] design — buildPortfolioSummary on holdings quoted in INR and USD returns a concentration number computed from weights that divide by the cross-currency totalMarketValue; the value is meaningless but carries no marker on the contract.
entries.evidence: [COD-portfolio-15] src/modules/portfolio/metrics.ts:150 (concentration from row.weight), 144-147 (weight divides by totalMarketValue), 70-71 (its doc carries no mixed-currency caveat); contrast 54-62 (totalMarketValue and totalPnl both document the D57 caveat explicitly) and src/modules/portfolio/PortfolioPanel.tsx:756-767 (the panel withholds it with a stated reason) -- refuter admitted (low->low): Confirmed. concentration = max(row.weight), where weight divides by the cross-currency totalMarketValue. Its doc ('Largest single-position weight') carries no D57 caveat, unlike totalMarketValue and totalPnl, and the panel alone withholds it. grep shows buildPortfolioSummary has no other production consumer today, so this is latent, low.

entries.fix_shape: Return concentration: null when mixedCurrencies (panel reads it), or document the caveat like its neighbours; pin with a mixed-currency metrics test.

entries.title: The 'atomic, crash-safe' note/export write never fsyncs (File::flush is a no-op), so the SC-032 survives-a-crash claim does not hold for the .md mirror
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-7] design — write_text_atomic does File::create -> write_all -> flush() -> rename with no sync_all on the file or the parent directory; on power loss the renamed file can appear with zero or partial content.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-7] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:303-309 (text) and :336-341 (bytes): `f.write_all(...)`, `f.flush()`, then `std::fs::rename`; std::fs::File's Write::flush is a documented no-op (File is unbuffered — it never fsyncs); doc comment src-tauri/src/lib.rs:281-286 claims 'the kernel rename(2) is atomic (SC-032: survives a crash mid-save)' -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real: both commands do File::create -> write_all -> flush -> rename with no sync_all on the file or directory (lib.rs:303-309, :336-341); File::flush does not fsync, so the SC-032 'survives a crash' comment (lib.rs:281-286) overclaims. Downgraded: the .md file is a mirror, not the note's primary store - notes-persistence.ts documents the workspace blob as 'the primary durable store' and the .md write as non-fatal (notes-persistence.ts:52,72-76), so a power-loss truncation of the mirror does not lose the note.
entries.root_cause: rename(2) is atomic for the directory entry, not the data; no sync_all on file or parent.
entries.fix_shape: f.sync_all()? before rename and (unix) sync the parent dir after, in the single write_atomic helper.

entries.title: write_text_atomic and write_bytes_atomic are the same 22 lines twice, so every durability or confinement fix must be made in both

entries.title: Dev keychain migration swallows a failed read and still sets migrated=true, so that secret is never retried and the report says success
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-11] Dev build, first boot, one account's keychain read errors on both passes (denied dialog / locked keychain) -> that secret is never copied, `migrated: true` is written, and the keychain is never read again by design. The report says already_done on every later boot.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-11] src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:286-292 (pass 2: `resolved.insert(account.clone(), read(account).unwrap_or(None))` — the error is discarded); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:197 (`store.migrated = true` runs unconditionally after the loop); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:180-186 and :258-264 (both guards then short-circuit forever); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:50-58 (MigrateReport has backend/migrated/already_done — no failed list, no error count); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:189-190 (the comment acknowledges the skip: 'the user re-adds it via Settings' — but nothing tells the user WHICH) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The logic defect is real: pass 2 converts a read error to None (keychain.rs:287-289), migrate_at then sets migrated=true unconditionally (keychain.rs:197-198), both guards short-circuit forever after (keychain.rs:180-186, :258-264), and MigrateReport has no failed list (keychain.rs:49-58). Corrected: the whole path is cfg(debug_assertions) (keychain.rs:92, :353-361) - no shipped user runs it - and nothing is 'forfeited': the secret stays in the OS keychain and the frontend treats migration as best-effort with Settings re-entry as the fallback (src/lib/keychain.ts:141-151). Dev-only edge: low.
entries.root_cause: Pass 2 converts a read error to None and the flag is set unconditionally; MigrateReport has no failed list. Debug-only path.
entries.fix_shape: Set migrated only when no read errored, or add failed: Vec<String> to MigrateReport and leave the flag unset; pin with a Rust unit test using an erroring reader.

entries.title: Dev keychain_migrate blocks an async-runtime worker for 140 s with no progress signal, so a dev first boot looks hung
entries.repro: [COD-rust-core-13] Dev build, first boot with existing OS-keychain items: keychain_migrate (an async command) calls std::thread::sleep(140s) inline; the renderer's invoke promise hangs for >2 minutes with no UI feedback.
entries.evidence: [COD-rust-core-13] src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:224 (MIGRATE_SELF_DISMISS_WAIT_SECS = 140); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:286 (std::thread::sleep inside migrate_collecting); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:348 (pub async fn keychain_migrate — runs on the Tauri async runtime); src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:354-360 (records that spawn_blocking was tried and broke the keychain read, so the inline placement is deliberate); the other three commands are async too (keychain.rs:299, :316, :332); docs/research/phase-10/hunt-rust-tauri.md BUG 6 flagged blocking keychain I/O on the async runtime and it is unfixed at 2d99cda -- refuter admitted (low->low): Holds as stated. keychain_migrate is an async command (keychain.rs:347-351) that runs migrate_collecting inline, which std::thread::sleep(140s) (keychain.rs:224, :286) on a Tauri async-runtime worker with no event/progress to the renderer; the inline placement is deliberate (keychain.rs:355-359) and the path is debug-only, so low is right.

entries.title: All three Rust child-kill closures hold the MutexGuard through the whole if-let body instead of releasing it after .take()
entries.repro: [INT-deferred-0-6] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:510 (main sidecar exit handler), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:188, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:185 each still write 'if let Some(child) = state.0.lock().unwrap().take() { let _ = child.kill(); }' -- the MutexGuard temporary from '.lock().unwrap()' lives for the whole if-let block (the clippy::significant_drop_in_scrutinee shape), not just for the .take() call.
entries.evidence: [INT-deferred-0-6] src-tauri/src/lib.rs:508-513, src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:186-192, src-tauri/src/sec_edgar_mcp.rs:183-189 -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): The pattern is present at all three sites (lib.rs:510, openbb_mcp.rs:188, sec_edgar_mcp.rs:185), and on edition 2021 (Cargo.toml:6) the guard does live through the if-let body. The claimed consequence does not hold, though. Each of these mutexes is locked in exactly one place, the kill path itself; grep finds no other lock() on SidecarProcess, OpenbbMcpProcess or SecEdgarMcpProcess. So no concurrent locker can be blocked. child.kill() only sends a signal and never re-enters the mutex, so there is no deadlock either. significant_drop_in_scrutinee is a nursery lint that clippy -D warnings does not enable. This is lint hygiene with zero behavioural effect: lowered from medium to low.
entries.root_cause: Edition-2021 temporary lifetime in an if-let scrutinee; no behavioural effect today (each mutex locked only here).
entries.fix_shape: let child = state.0.lock().unwrap().take(); if let Some(child) = child { ... } at the three sites.

entries.title: The server code node admits unbounded ** and list * and evaluates synchronously on the event loop (7**10**7 blocked the sidecar 8.2 s), reachable via MCP run_workflow
entries.repro: [COD-workflow-engine-7] evaluate_code({}, {'expression': '7**(10**7)'}) took 8.226 s on the event loop (7**10**6: 0.2 s; growth is super-linear, 7**10**8 is minutes). '[0]*10**9' is also admitted (ast.List + BinOp Mult). Reachable by an agent through MCP run_workflow/save_workflow.
entries.evidence: [COD-workflow-engine-7] sidecar/services/workflow_nodes/code_node.py:5-6 ('Safe by construction'), :20-27 (ast.Pow, ast.Mult unbounded), :62-63, :84-85, :89-100 (sync evaluation inside an async handler, no to_thread, no size guard) -- refuter admitted_with_correction (medium->low): Real: ast.Pow and ast.Mult are unbounded and evaluation runs synchronously inside the async handler on the event loop (7**10**6 took 0.21 s here; larger exponents grow super-linearly). Downgraded: it needs a pathological expression authored by the local user or their own agent in a single-user local app, and the node editor evaluates code nodes client-side, so only the MCP/agent path reaches it - not something hit in normal use.
entries.root_cause: 'Safe by construction' covers code execution, not CPU/memory exhaustion.
entries.fix_shape: Bound Pow exponents, reject Mult on list/str operands, evaluate via asyncio.to_thread with a timeout; pin with a test that 7**(10**7) is rejected fast.
